title: Routing provenance and reconciliation patterns for control plane data model
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a pragmatic approach for modeling resources, environment overlays, region/cluster bindings, and composable routing policies in the control plane. It focuses on provenance (who changed what), reconciliation and healing loops, and concrete CRUD API patterns that preserve safety across multi-region deployment and operator workflows.

Background and goals:
- We must support: global resource metadata, environment-scoped overrides (dev/staging/prod), region/cluster binding for placement, and runtime routing rules used by the serving layer.
- Requirements: strong audit/provenance, eventual consistency with idempotent APIs, conflict resolution strategy for concurrent operators, minimal coupling to runtime, and clear failure semantics for clients.

Key ideas (summary):
1) Resource as layered descriptor: canonical "resource" is the single source-of-truth (global). Each resource can have zero or more "overlays" per environment. Overlays store only diffs/overrides.
2) Bindings are first-class: region/cluster bindings are separate records that reference resource + environment and carry placement metadata (capacity hints, allowed instance types).
3) Routing policy composition: policies are small composable units (selector -> action). A routing policy document is evaluated left-to-right by priority with explicit fallbacks.
4) Provenance metadata: every change includes actor, actor-type (human/service), timestamp, reason, and change-set id. Keep last-applied op metadata for reconciliation.
5) Reconciliation loop: control plane persists intended state; a reconciler projects intended -> observed and drives repair actions. Reconciler must use stable IDs and ETags to avoid loops.

Data model primitives (conceptual):
- Resource: {id, kind, owner, global_spec, created_by, created_at, last_modified, last_change_id}
- Overlay: {id, resource_id, environment, patch, last_modified, modified_by}
- Binding: {id, resource_id, environment, region, cluster_id, placement_constraints, capacity_hint, status}
- RoutingPolicy: {id, name, priority, selector, action, fallback_policy_id, provenance}
- Provenance record: {change_id, actor, actor_type, ts, origin_ticket}
(we store these as flat fields; above is conceptual only)

Routing policy semantics: composition & evaluation
- Policies are evaluated in priority order. Each policy has a selector (labels, request attributes) and an action (route to binding, rewrite, weight-based split).
- Actions may reference binding ids or tag expressions. When an action references a binding, resolution happens at evaluation time; missing bindings trigger defined fallback behavior.
- Policies are composable: a policy may delegate to another policy (fallback_policy_id). Delegations are explicit and limited to a small depth to avoid cycles.
- Cycle prevention: control plane detects cycles on create/update and rejects with 409 + explanation.

CRUD API patterns (REST examples and semantics):
- Create resource: POST /v1/resources {kind, global_spec, owner} -> 201 {id, etag, created_at}
  - Idempotency: client may provide Idempotency-Key header; server attaches change_id and returns. If same key previously accepted, return existing change result.
- Read resource: GET /v1/resources/{id} -> 200 {resource, overlays:[], bindings:[], etag}
- Update resource: PATCH /v1/resources/{id} {patch} -> 200 {etag, change_id}
  - Concurrency: server supports If-Match: <etag> for optimistic concurrency. Patch applies server-side JSON-Patch/merge semantics.
- Create overlay: POST /v1/resources/{id}/overlays {environment, patch} -> 201 {overlay_id}
- Create binding: POST /v1/resources/{id}/bindings {environment, region, cluster_id, placement_constraints} -> 201 {binding_id}
- Update binding status (reconciler): PATCH /v1/bindings/{binding_id}/status {status, observed_at} -> 200
- Routing policy CRUD: POST /v1/policies {name, priority, selector, action, fallback_policy_id} -> 201

Errors and expected semantics:
- 409 conflict when resource version mismatch or detected policy cycle.
- 400 for invalid selectors or unresolved references.
- 424 failed dependency when a referenced binding is in an error state and request cannot proceed.
- 202 accepted for requests that kick off async placement/reconciliation with link to status resource (/v1/ops/{op_id}).

Idempotency & change ids:
- Every client-changing operation generates a change_id (opaque). Change_id is recorded in provenance and used by reconciler to reason about whether an observed state matches intended state.
- Support Idempotency-Key header for create operations. Duplicate creates return the resource created in the first request.

Reconciliation, eventual consistency, and backoff:
- Reconcilers read intended state (resources + overlays + bindings + policies) and attempt to converge observed state.
- Use exponential backoff + jitter on retry. State transitions are guarded by ETags/change ids to avoid stepping on concurrent manual updates.
- Store last_reconciled_change_id on binding/status to short-circuit repeated reconciliation attempts.

Provenance and audit trails:
- All writes attach provenance (actor, ticket, change_id). Provide GET /v1/resources/{id}/history?limit=50 to view changes.
- For governance, export of provenance to audit log sink (immutable append-only store) is supported via async job.

Operational considerations and SLOs:
- API latency SLOs for reads (single-region): p50 < 20ms, p95 < 120ms.
- Reconciliation lag SLO: 95% of simple binding creates reconciled within 30s; complex placements (cross-region) within 2m.
- Rate limits: per-tenant write QPS caps documented; large bulk operations should use bulk endpoints (/v1/bulk/..).

Migration and compatibility:
- New overlay model is backward-compatible: existing global-only resources map to environment="prod" overlay implicitly until migrated.
- Client library should prefer PATCH with If-Match to avoid races.

Testing and verification:
- Unit tests for selector evaluation and fallback chain.
- Integration tests simulate network partitions: ensure reconciler does not flip-flop state after transient failures.
- Chaos test: inject delayed binding resolution to verify policy fallback behavior.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Strong vs eventual consistency: we choose eventual consistency to keep runtime availability high, but expose clear reconciliation progress to callers.
- Transactional multi-resource updates: do we need cross-resource atomicity? For now, avoid; provide bulk ops with best-effort rollback and explicit op ids.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Prototype policy evaluation library and unit test selector language by 2026-03.
- Draft an API compatibility guide for SDKs describing ETag usage and idempotency-key patterns.
- Add a small service that exports provenance to the analytics/audit bucket (PLAT-1423).

Notes: this doc is a working sketch for discussion. Key focus areas for reviewers: policy composition semantics, change_id usage, and reconciliation short-circuiting heuristics.
summary: Working sketch for layered resource + overlay model, first-class bindings, composable routing policies, provenance and reconciliation-driven control plane APIs.
